items.title: Molly Meldrum, Australian music presenter and Countdown host, dies at 83
items.why: Ian 'Molly' Meldrum died in hospital in Melbourne on Monday morning after a period of declining health, his management said. He hosted ABC TV's music show Countdown from 1974 to 1987, helping to launch Australian acts and bring stars such as ABBA and Madonna to Australian audiences.
items.matters: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and many musicians paid tribute to a figure who shaped Australian pop for decades.

items.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992 after recount
items.why: Democrat Chuck Hubbard won North Carolina's 5th district after a recount, beating long-serving Republican Virginia Foxx by about 330 votes. That gives Democrats at least 258 of the 435 House seats in the November midterms, their most since 1992. Four races are still undecided.
items.matters: A large majority lets Democrats control the House agenda and investigations for the second half of President Trump's term.

items.title: Alcaraz beats Zverev to win his first ATP Finals title
items.why: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev of Germany 6-2, 7-6 in the ATP Finals final in Turin, Italy, on Sunday. He saved three set points in the tie-break and won all five of his matches. It is his 30th career title.
items.matters: He joins Agassi, Federer and Djokovic as the only men to win all four majors and the season-ending finals.

items.title: Liverpool beat ten-man Manchester United 4-0 in Pochettino's first game
items.why: Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday in Mauricio Pochettino's first match as United manager. Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz scored. United are 19th in the Premier League.

items.title: Marc Márquez clinches eighth MotoGP world title in Portugal
items.why: Spain's Marc Márquez finished eighth at the Portuguese Grand Prix in Portimão on Sunday, enough to win his eighth premier-class title with one race left. Italy's Marco Bezzecchi won the race. Márquez had been 102 points behind Bezzecchi earlier in the season.
items.matters: He equals Giacomo Agostini's record of eight top-class titles and moves past Valentino Rossi's seven.

items.title: Gukesh and Sindarov open youngest-ever world chess title match in Geneva
items.why: India's Gukesh Dommaraju defends his world chess title against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva, Switzerland. The opening ceremony is on Sunday and the first game on Tuesday 24 November. Both are 20, making it the youngest title match ever. The first to 7.5 points from 14 games wins.
items.matters: Sindarov is unbeaten against Gukesh in classical games; a win would make him Uzbekistan's first undisputed world champion.

items.title: Verstappen wins chaotic Las Vegas Grand Prix from pole
items.why: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix by 0.639 seconds from McLaren's Lando Norris, with Oscar Piastri third. New champion Kimi Antonelli lost two places on the final lap to finish fourth. Ferrari team-mates Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc collided again.
items.matters: It was Verstappen's 75th career win and lifts him to second in the drivers' standings.
items.changed: Updated: the race has been run and Verstappen won

items.title: Indonesia sweets factory fire kills at least three; dozens unaccounted for
items.why: A fire at a sweets factory in Cikande, in Banten province west of Jakarta, has killed at least three people, officials say. Police have recovered several body bags; identifying victims by DNA could take weeks. Officials give differing counts of missing workers, from 29 to about 50.
items.changed: Updated: more remains recovered; official counts of missing workers differ

items.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv region kill at least 12, Ukraine says
items.why: Russian overnight strikes on Sunday killed at least 12 people in Ukraine's Kyiv region, officials say. The regional governor says nine died when an apartment block partly collapsed in Dymer, north of the capital. Rescuers are searching for 11 missing people, including two children.
items.matters: President Zelensky says Russia fired about 2,700 drones and 165 missiles at Ukraine this week.
items.changed: Updated: the death toll rose to at least 12 and a child was pulled out alive

items.title: Russian warship hit by suspected drone attack at Libya's Benghazi port
items.why: A Russian navy corvette, the Merkury, was hit at dawn on Sunday while docked in Benghazi, eastern Libya, causing an explosion and fire, the eastern-based government says. Libyan military officials blame Ukrainian sea drones. Satellite images show the ship partly sunk. No one has claimed responsibility.
items.matters: It follows Saturday's drone strike on a Russian cargo ship in the Baltic, suggesting the war is reaching further from Ukraine.

items.title: South Korea's education minister resigns over AI exam cheating fears
items.why: Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday, and President Lee Jae Myung accepted. He took responsibility for last-minute rules to stop AI-assisted cheating in Thursday's Suneung university entrance exam. Officials say 111 test-takers were caught with smart devices.
items.matters: It began when a top scorer in a national accountancy exam admitted using a hidden camera and phone.

items.title: India post record 720-9 in first Test against New Zealand
items.why: India declared on 720 for nine at the Basin Reserve in Wellington, New Zealand, the highest Test total ever made in the country. KL Rahul scored 136 and Rishabh Pant 128. New Zealand closed day four on 119 for two, 233 runs behind.

items.title: Drone strikes kill four in Sudan's capital and damage UN building
items.why: Drone attacks early on Sunday killed at least four people in and around Khartoum, Sudan's capital, according to local reports, and damaged a UN building with staff inside, the UN says. The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces were blamed. Sudan's army says the drones came from Ethiopia, which denies it.

items.title: Settlers set Palestinian cars on fire in West Bank villages, reports say
items.why: Israeli settlers set fire to about 12 vehicles and sprayed slogans on homes in Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan, near Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, early on Sunday, Palestinian sources say. Israel's army condemned the attacks and police opened an investigation.

items.title: Bahrain says Iranian strike wounded two; Iran says tankers hit mines
items.why: Bahrain's interior ministry says an Iranian strike on a civilian industrial site on Saturday wounded two people, one critically. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they targeted US air-defence systems. On Sunday Iranian forces said two tankers caught fire after hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia condemned the attacks.
items.matters: The strait carries a large share of the world's oil, so attacks there affect energy prices everywhere.
items.changed: Updated: Bahrain says two people were wounded; Iran reports tankers hit by mines

items.title: BepiColombo spacecraft enters orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
items.why: The European–Japanese BepiColombo mission entered orbit around Mercury on Saturday after a 37-minute engine burn, the European Space Agency says. It launched in 2018. The burn ended early because of a software issue, but ESA says the spacecraft is safe. Its two orbiters separate on 9–10 December.
items.matters: It is only the second mission to orbit Mercury, the planet closest to the Sun; science work starts in April 2027.

items.title: England beat New Zealand 37-12 for record win over All Blacks
items.why: England scored five tries to beat New Zealand 37-12 at Twickenham in London on Saturday in the Nations Championship. The 25-point margin is England's largest against the All Blacks and New Zealand's heaviest defeat in the northern hemisphere.

items.title: EU and Indonesia sign trade deal after ten years of talks
items.why: The European Union and Indonesia signed a trade agreement and an investment protection deal in Brussels on Saturday. Indonesia says 90.4% of its goods will enter the EU duty-free. The EU gains easier access to a market of 280 million people and to nickel for batteries.
items.matters: Both sides still need to ratify it; Indonesia expects it to take effect in 2027.

items.title: Brazil's former president Bolsonaro in intensive care with bowel blockage
items.why: Jair Bolsonaro, 71, is in intensive care at a hospital in Brazil's capital, Brasília, with an intestinal obstruction, the hospital said on Saturday. It says he is stable and conscious. He is serving a 27-year sentence for a coup plot under house arrest; he denies the charges.

items.title: Mexico captures FBI-wanted cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro' in Sinaloa
items.why: Mexican forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, an alleged Beltrán Leyva cartel leader on the FBI's ten most wanted list, in Guasave, Sinaloa, on Friday night. Mexico's military says seven gunmen and four soldiers were killed in the firefight. Roadblocks were later set up across the state.
items.matters: He faces charges in Mexico and the US, where a $5m reward had been offered for him.

items.title: Swimmer braves Strait of Hormuz to highlight war's harm to wildlife
items.why: British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh, a UN Patron of the Oceans, swam about 15km in stages over three days from Oman's Musandam Peninsula around the Cape of Hormuz. He says he saw tankers hit nearby. He warns pollution could harm coral reefs, mangroves, turtles and dolphins.

items.title: EU budget plan proposes a 3% tax on big tech companies
items.why: European Council President António Costa on Saturday proposed a 2028–2034 EU budget €204bn smaller than the Commission's plan. It includes a 3% levy on large firms' EU revenue from online advertising, digital services and user data, plus taxes on e-waste and tobacco. Several governments have criticised it.
items.matters: Tax changes need every EU country to agree, and the levy could anger the US government.

items.title: Drones set Russian cargo ship on fire in Gulf of Finland
items.why: Russian officials say two drones hit the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship Sparta II on Saturday, setting it on fire. All 16 crew were evacuated. Finland's armed forces say Ukraine was likely behind it; Ukraine has not commented. On Sunday Russian vessels towed the ship out of Finnish waters, Finland's president said.
items.matters: Finland's prime minister, Petteri Orpo, said 'war is spilling over into our immediate vicinity'.
items.changed: Updated: the ship has been towed out of Finnish waters

items.title: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, South Africa's first woman deputy president, dies at 71
items.why: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka died on Friday evening of complications from a medical procedure about two weeks earlier, her family said. She was South Africa's deputy president from 2005 to 2008 and led UN Women from 2013 to 2021.
items.matters: President Cyril Ramaphosa and UN chief António Guterres led tributes to a long-time campaigner for women's rights.

items.title: Toxic alcohol kills at least 17 in India's Manipur state, officials say
items.why: At least 17 people have died since mid-November in India's north-eastern Manipur state after drinking suspected bootleg liquor, a state government spokesperson said. Hundreds were treated in hospitals in the state capital, Imphal, some needing dialysis. Six people have been arrested and an inquiry ordered.

items.title: Russian missile strike on Zelensky's hometown kills two, wounds 60
items.why: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kryvyi Rih in central Ukraine on Friday night. Local officials say a seven-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman were killed and 60 people were wounded, including six children. About 25 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools were damaged, the city's head says.

items.title: Cricket Australia gives Pat Cummins unanimous backing as Test captain
items.why: Cricket Australia's board says Pat Cummins keeps its 'unanimous support' as captain, after former teammates Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft said the 2018 ball-tampering plot was widely known. Cummins denies knowing. The board ruled out a new inquiry but set up a forum for players to share accounts.
items.matters: Separately, Fox Cricket says Khawaja and David Warner will be 'rested' from its commentary for the coming weeks.

items.title: Nations agree to work on rules for AI 'killer robots' by 2028
items.why: At UN-backed talks in Geneva, the 128 states in the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons agreed early on Saturday to 'elaborate' an instrument on lethal autonomous weapons over two years. Nearly 100 countries wanted binding rules sooner; campaigners say the US and Russia blocked stronger wording.
items.matters: Weapons that choose and attack targets without a human decision are already being developed and tested.

items.title: US media report hacks at FBI crime database and farm agency
items.why: The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its National Crime Information Center, used by police across the US, NBC News and CNN reported on Friday. Separately, a US Department of Agriculture system for paying farmers was hit by a cyberattack, officials said. It is unclear who is responsible.
items.matters: The FBI database holds warrant and background-check records used by police every day.

items.title: Poland says Russian missiles crashed on its soil near European drills
items.why: Poland says two Russian missiles and a drone fell on its territory on Friday during an attack on Ukraine, near Nowy Lipowiec, about 60km from the Ukrainian border. Nobody was hurt. In Warsaw on Saturday, NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance 'will defend every inch of Polish territory'.
items.matters: NATO's North Atlantic Council meets on Monday to discuss the incident, which Poland calls a deliberate provocation.
items.changed: Updated: NATO's chief pledged to defend Poland; NATO ambassadors meet in Brussels on Monday
Updated: reactions from the UN chief and governments
items.title: COP31 climate talks in Türkiye end without a deal over fossil fuels
items.why: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Sunday, two days late, without an agreed final text. The EU and small island states rejected a draft that did not mention fossil fuels, which Saudi Arabia and Russia had opposed. UN chief António Guterres said he was 'deeply disappointed'.
items.matters: Al Jazeera says it is the first UN climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009 to end without a deal adopted by all.
